title: Hampton's band ends and Moore sets out for New York
summary: Musicians urged him to go to New York; the trombone was last hired in California bands, and when Hampton left for Goodman he headed east but stalled in Arizona.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I see. How did that -- how did you get the recommendation for that band?

I -- through the grapevine, most of it. I hear musicians tell me, "Chief, you sound so good; why don't you go to New York? New York's the place for you." They said, "You should go to New York." You know. One reason why a trombonist in California, a -- most groups that form consist of the rhythm section, and I, and I,and a, was only four pieces, and there's no place for a trombone. A trombone in California is, was the, the first to be hired, -- what, what was I saying? -- and, and the last to be fired.
Last hired and the first fired.

Last hired and first fired; I, I meant -- that's what I meant. Anyway, I, -- at that time I couldn't -- I made a nice living all right because I was doin' pretty good, and, until, until a, Hampton closed his -- he got his break with Benny Goodman. And once more I roamed the

streets of Los Angeles, and pretty soon my money -- I got little property at home on the reservation, and money came, and I cut out. And I said well here I come New York. And I got as far as the reservation in -- south of Phoenix, back to Pima land, and I gave all my money to my mother, and I got stranded there.
